Hi Oliver / Sofia,

Great to meet with you this morning — thanks for the time. Per our discovery, I wanted to summarize the key items we covered and call out a few follow-ups specific to ACME Bank's data residency and PII requirements so we can qualify and scope properly.

Recap / asks from our side:
- Primary requirement: production inference for customer-facing flows must ensure PII (names, account numbers, SSNs) never leaves EU data centers.
- Secondary: acceptable cross-region failover behavior (automatic vs manual) and backup storage location (same region vs cross-region).
- Audit/logging: required retention for request/response logs and admin audit trails (you mentioned 3 years as a possible target).
- Compliance: SOC 2 and DPA will be required as part of procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a short note with our region pinning options, default backup behavior, and logging retention configs.
2) Share SOC 2 summary and architecture diagram (attached).
3) Schedule a technical call with Sean (solutions engineer) to go over recovery / failover modes and encryption details — suggested times below.

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-faq.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, draft arch diagram (inline).

Proposed times for a 30m deep-dive with Sean: Tue 31 Mar 09:30-10:00 PT, Tue 31 Mar 14:00-14:30 PT, Wed 1 Apr 11:00-11:30 PT. Let me know what works for you.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on the constraints so we can include the residency terms in the upcoming SOW.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Aditya,

Thanks for the recap — helpful. A few clarifying questions so we can confirm the requirement set for procurement: 

1) Cross-region failover: Our security/compliance team prefers failover that does not promote a non-EU region to primary without explicit approval. Is Redwood able to support manual approval for failover, or can you guarantee that failovers will still restrict PII to EU?

2) Backups: Are automated backups stored in the same region by default? If backups are ever replicated cross-region (for DR), what controls do we have to ensure PII is excluded or encrypted under our KMS?

3) Logs/audit: We will likely require at least 12 months of request/response metadata and 3 years for admin audit logs. What is Redwood's default retention and can it be configured?

Also — please send the SOC 2 report and the architecture diagram (the team will want to see how keys and network isolation are handled).

Regards,
Oliver

Oliver — thanks, great questions. Short answers below and I've included more detail in the attachments and the architecture diagram. I also flagged the technical questions for Sean so he can cover them on the call.

1) Region pinning / failover
- Redwood supports region pinning to a specific region (US, EU, APAC) at the customer or environment level.
- Failover behavior: By default we provide "pinned-primary with controlled failover" — automatic failover is available for latency/availability SLAs, but can be disabled. For regulated customers we support manual approval workflows for cross-region promotion (we'll only promote after an explicit admin approval step).
- If manual-only failover is requested, we can implement a policy that prevents any PII-bearing workloads from being routed to non-EU capacity during failover unless explicit approval is granted.

2) Backups & DR
- Automated snapshot backups are stored in the same pinned region by default and are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys (CMKs) where requested.
- Cross-region backups are optional and require an explicit config/contract change. If cross-region replication is enabled, we offer filters so customers can exclude PII from replicated backups; alternatively, we can encrypt replicated backups under your KMS in the destination region.

3) Logs & retention
- Default retention: request/response metadata (30 days), admin audit logs (90 days).
- Configurable retention tiers are available as an add-on — we can provide 12 months for request metadata and 3 years for admin audit logs per your ask. Retention changes are recorded in the audit trail and are reversible only with admin approval.

Other controls:
- All data in-flight and at-rest is encrypted (TLS + AES-256).
- Private deployments (VPC/Private) provide network isolation; for ACME we can discuss Private deployment options if the procurement team prefers.
- We can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key control and provide audit logs for key operations.

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-faq.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, rdw-arch-diagram.png
